meta.name: Housing Policy Evidence Ontology
meta.description: Typed graph of the team's literature and data review: benchmark scenarios, expert domains, outcome measures, causal mechanisms, datasets, and studies, with the links between them. Built from the team research memo (Literature & data review), the combined research workbook (Studies sheet, 77 entries), research/papers/README.md, and research/data/*.md.
meta.license_note: This file is first-party metadata (Apache-2.0). It describes third-party studies and datasets but contains none of their content beyond short factual summaries. A dataset's license_status governs whether the submission may depend on it; see AGENTS.md section 2.

license_status.open_verified: Public domain or explicit unrestricted open license, with a provenance file in research/data/. Usable.
license_status.unverified: Mentioned by a study or the team memo; license not yet checked. Not usable until a provenance file passes the license rule.
license_status.proprietary: Commercial or paywalled. Not usable (Official Rules section 7.b.iii).
license_status.restricted: Access limited to some user classes. Not usable (section 10.5).
license_status.rejected_share_alike: ODbL / CC BY-SA style terms. Removed (section 7.b.ii).
license_status.rejected_unclear: Terms conflict or are unstated after checking. Removed until clarified.

evidence_type.causal_quasi_experimental: Difference-in-differences, synthetic control, regression discontinuity, event study.
evidence_type.structural_model: Estimated or calibrated equilibrium or dynamic model with counterfactuals.
evidence_type.associational: Panel or cross-sectional association without a clean counterfactual.
evidence_type.survey: Owner, developer or planner surveys and interviews.
evidence_type.measurement: Builds a regulation index, corpus, data model or input measure.
evidence_type.framework: Modeling framework or software without a quantified policy effect.

verification.primary_text_checked: Primary text (paper or report) read for the stated finding.
verification.secondary_summary: Only a summary by another party was read.
verification.citation_only: Bibliographic identity checked; no finding certified.

scenarios.label: Baseline (current rules)
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Current rules, no policy change, over a five-year horizon, using the same economic assumptions as the reform scenarios.

scenarios.label: Scenario 1: Accessory dwelling units
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Allow one ADU on parcels with single-family homes, at least 600 sq ft, with no added parking requirement.

scenarios.label: Scenario 2: Missing middle (2-6 units)
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Allow 2-6 units on single-family parcels, up to three stories.

scenarios.label: Scenario 3: Transit-oriented density
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Higher density near major transit stops, with a justified proximity threshold.

scenarios.label: Scenario 4: Parking reduction
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Reduce or eliminate minimum parking requirements, with explicit assumptions about developer-provided parking.

scenarios.label: Scenario 5: Development fee reduction
scenarios.benchmark_definition: Cut development fees by 50%, assuming $50,000 per unit in total fees (a challenge assumption, not observed local fee data).

domains.label: Accessory dwelling units
domains.description: ADU legalization, owner uptake, financing, local implementation of state preemption, and permitted vs. occupied ADUs.

domains.label: Missing middle (2-6 units)
domains.description: Duplex-to-sixplex legalization on single-family lots, lot splits (SB 9), feasibility vs. uptake, broad upzoning comparisons.

domains.label: Transit-oriented density
domains.description: Upzoning near transit, stop definitions and proximity thresholds, entitlement risk, binding density constraints.

domains.label: Parking requirements
domains.description: Minimum parking repeal, voluntary developer parking, parking construction costs, and state parking preemption.

domains.label: Development and impact fees
domains.description: Impact fee incidence, fee levels and design, infrastructure funding effects, and the 50% fee-cut benchmark.

domains.label: Baseline, data and provenance
domains.description: Datasets, licenses, provenance, the five-year baseline, permits vs. starts vs. completions, and pilot-state data availability.

domains.label: Modeling, interactions and uncertainty
domains.description: Model architecture (pro forma + uptake + timing), policy interactions, uncertainty ranges, validation, and what not to add together.

outcomes.label: Units authorized by permit
outcomes.note: Not starts or completions; some permitted units are never built.

outcomes.label: Housing starts
outcomes.note: Many studies labeled 'starts' actually measure permits or consents.

outcomes.label: Completed units
outcomes.note: Lagged from permits; the Survey of Construction gives regional lag factors.

outcomes.label: Net housing stock
outcomes.note: Completions minus demolitions/losses; the challenge allows stock or production as the outcome.

outcomes.label: Market-feasible capacity
outcomes.note: Units that would pencil financially; not a forecast of uptake.

outcomes.label: Modeled expected units
outcomes.note: Capacity times a modeled development probability.

outcomes.label: Applications or proposed units
outcomes.note: Attrition to permits can be large (see Kestelman 2025).

outcomes.label: Parking spaces supplied
outcomes.note: A parking reduction is not a housing-unit increase.

outcomes.label: Prices and rents
outcomes.note: Price effects are not unit counts.

outcomes.label: Floorspace
outcomes.note: Floorspace growth is not an equal percentage growth in homes.

mechanisms.label: Legal eligibility
mechanisms.description: Which parcels the reform newly allows to build, net of what baseline zoning already permits.

mechanisms.label: Binding constraint
mechanisms.description: A relaxed rule only matters if it was the constraint that bound; other rules (density, height, lot size) may still bind.

mechanisms.label: Financial feasibility
mechanisms.description: Whether a project pencils given rents/prices, hard and soft costs, fees, parking and financing.

mechanisms.label: Owner or developer uptake
mechanisms.description: Share of feasible parcels whose owners actually build, over time.

mechanisms.label: Financing capacity
mechanisms.description: Owner equity and credit access, especially for ADUs.

mechanisms.label: Local implementation
mechanisms.description: Heterogeneous, sometimes resistant, local responses to state preemption.

mechanisms.label: Entitlement risk and attrition
mechanisms.description: Proposed and approved units that never reach permit.

mechanisms.label: Permit-to-completion timing
mechanisms.description: Lags and attrition from permit to start to completion within five years.

mechanisms.label: Regional displacement
mechanisms.description: Local gains partly relocate construction from elsewhere in the region; statewide totals must be net.

mechanisms.label: Voluntary parking
mechanisms.description: Developers keep supplying parking after minimums are repealed when the market demands it.

mechanisms.label: Fee incidence
mechanisms.description: Who bears fees: buyers, developers, or landowners through lower land prices.

mechanisms.label: Infrastructure funding
mechanisms.description: Fees can fund infrastructure or substitute for exclusionary approvals, so cutting them can have offsetting effects.

mechanisms.label: Legalization vs. new construction
mechanisms.description: ADU permits can legalize existing units rather than add new ones.

studies.title: Terner Housing Policy Simulator: Full Methodology
studies.finding: Combines parcel pro formas with a historical logistic development-probability model; expected units equal optimal project units times development probability. Has explicit missing-middle, transit, parking and half-fee scenarios.
studies.limitation: Historical calibration is not out-of-sample validation; expected units are not a causal effect or five-year starts.
studies.relevance: Closest template for our pipeline: eligible parcels, feasible projects, development probability, expected units. Add permit-to-start timing, demolitions, interactions and held-out validation.

studies.title: The Effect of Local Government Policies on Housing Supply
studies.finding: Dynamic pro forma producing modeled project-build probabilities from 0-99%, applied to San Francisco, Oakland, Pleasanton and Menlo Park.
studies.limitation: Simulated potential production, not observed starts; 2016 assumptions need updating.
studies.relevance: Supports our policy sensitivity design; treat the 0-99% probability as a modeling choice, not a validated rate.

studies.title: Supply Constraints and Housing Market Dynamics
studies.finding: Regulatory delay and marginal costs reduce supply responsiveness; geographic constraints affect investment levels.
studies.limitation: Permit-based investment measures; regulatory index does not identify our five reforms.
studies.relevance: Use a dynamic baseline that separates policy from demand, rates, geography and delays.

studies.title: Land Use Regulation and New Construction
studies.authors: Christopher J. Mayer; C. Tsuriel Somerville
studies.finding: More regulation is associated with lower construction and supply elasticity; delay-related restrictions have larger effects than fee indicators.
studies.limitation: Permits proxy for starts; observational comparisons, not randomized reforms.
studies.relevance: Model approval time separately from direct fees; don't use as a causal fee coefficient.

studies.title: Estimating the Economic Value of Zoning Reform
studies.authors: Santosh Anagol; Fernando Ferreira; Jonah Rexer
studies.finding: Sao Paulo corridor densification increased multifamily filings; the published equilibrium model estimates aggregate stock 1.6% higher and prices 0.4% lower.
studies.limitation: Modeled stock effect, not starts. Don't combine with the older working-paper figures (1.9% stock, -0.5% prices).
studies.relevance: Strong example linking a density reform to citywide stock; use the 2026 published estimates; recalibrate for U.S. settings.

studies.title: Evaluating the Long-Run Effects of Zoning Reform on Urban Development
studies.venue: EPC working paper 013 (2025 journal version exists)
studies.finding: Land-price gradients imply roughly an 18% long-run floorspace increase from Auckland upzoning (draft).
studies.limitation: Floorspace is not unit count; reconcile with the 2025 journal version.
studies.relevance: Long-run density mechanism; not a five-year starts forecast.

studies.title: UrbanSim: Modeling Urban Development for Land Use, Transportation, and Environmental Planning
studies.finding: Statistical simulation of real-estate development under policy scenarios.
studies.limitation: No quantified policy effect; documentation doesn't validate any implementation.
studies.relevance: Candidate architecture only if data and validation justify the complexity.

studies.title: A 3D agent-based model for simulating urban densification in Toronto, Canada
studies.authors: Richard Burke; Raja Sengupta; Alistair Ford
studies.venue: EPB: Urban Analytics and City Science (online June 2024)
studies.finding: Agent-based scenarios of residents, developers, landowners and zoning authority, with unit outcomes through 2040.
studies.limitation: Scenario forecasts, not causal; no five-year result or external validation.
studies.relevance: Alternative simulation architecture; needs a transparent calibration strategy.

studies.title: The Effects of Residential Zoning in U.S. Housing Markets
studies.finding: Infers minimum lot sizes from construction bunching; 18.5% of single-family construction bunches at regulated thresholds.
studies.limitation: Measures binding rules; not a reform response. Proprietary data.
studies.relevance: Way to infer binding minimum-lot rules where zoning data are incomplete.

studies.title: Evaluating California's Accessory Dwelling Unit Reforms: Preliminary Evidence and Lessons for State Governments
studies.authors: Nicholas J. Marantz; Christopher S. Elmendorf; Youjin B. Kim
studies.finding: Larger parcels and multiple existing structures predict ADU permitting; rent and HOA associations are heterogeneous.
studies.limitation: Associations, not a causal statewide effect; permits can legalize existing ADUs; proprietary inputs.
studies.relevance: Highest-priority ADU input: predictors of where permitting occurs and a parcel-data recipe. Separate legalizations from new construction.

studies.title: ADU Update: Early Lessons and Impacts of California's State and Local Policy Changes
studies.finding: Substantial increases in ADU applications and permits after state and local reforms.
studies.limitation: No counterfactual; applications and permits are mixed; partial-year 2017 data.
studies.relevance: Early implementation barriers; harmonize applications vs. permits before comparing.

studies.title: Jumpstarting the Market for Accessory Dwelling Units: Lessons Learned from Portland, Seattle and Vancouver
studies.authors: Karen Chapple; Jake Wegmann; Farzad Mashhood; Rebecca Coleman
studies.finding: Owner surveys (1,837 contacted, 414 responses) document finance and implementation barriers to ADUs.
studies.limitation: Surveys successful permitted owners; nonresponse bias.
studies.relevance: Design ADU uptake assumptions and sensitivity cases around finance and owner capacity.

studies.title: Transforming Homeowners into Landlords: A Survey of Homeowners with Accessory Dwelling Units in Los Angeles
studies.finding: Examines whether permitted ADUs become long-term housing; supports distinguishing permits from occupied supply.
studies.limitation: Owner-reported uses; no net-supply estimate.
studies.relevance: Add occupancy/use checks; a permit is not an automatic net addition.

studies.title: Accessory Dwelling Units Can Meaningfully Boost Housing Supply
studies.finding: Cities under permissive ADU laws issued 81 ADU permits per 100,000 residents in 2025; outside California the figure was 26.
studies.limitation: Descriptive cross-city differences; California dominates aggregates. These are total ADU permits in cities of 100,000+ residents, not the additional permits a new law causes, and smaller towns and rural areas are not covered; treat 26 (outside California) and 81 as rough low and high anchors for a gross rate, not a net effect.
studies.relevance: Cross-city ADU benchmark; report California separately and match policy details to the 600 sq ft / no-parking scenario.

studies.title: Will Allowing Duplexes and Lot Splits on Parcels Zoned for Single-Family Create New Homes?
studies.authors: Ben Metcalf; David Garcia; Ian Carlton; Kate Macfarlane
studies.finding: SB 9 enables new development on 5.4% of single-family parcels, about 700,000 additional market-feasible units; development is infeasible on about 80% of parcels either way.
studies.limitation: Financially feasible capacity, not a forecast of starts or uptake.
studies.relevance: Key missing-middle feasibility example: large feasible capacity can coexist with low uptake.

studies.title: California's HOME Act Turns One: Data and Insights from the First Year of Senate Bill 9
studies.finding: Limited early SB 9 use: Los Angeles received 211 new-unit applications in 2022, San Diego seven.
studies.limitation: First-year applications in 13 selected jurisdictions; not starts or causal.
studies.relevance: Reality check on missing-middle uptake; supports gradual adoption.

studies.title: Middle Housing in the Single-Dwelling Zones, Progress Report 2018-2024
studies.authors: Cascadia Partners; Portland Bureau of Planning and Sustainability
studies.finding: Over 1,400 ADU and middle-housing units permitted in single-dwelling zones from August 2021 through June 2024.
studies.limitation: Observed post-reform permitting, not causal.
studies.relevance: U.S. implementation evidence; separate the two housing types and compare to a baseline trend.

studies.title: The impact of upzoning on housing construction in Auckland
studies.finding: Preferred spillover-adjusted calculation attributes 21,808 additional dwelling permits over five years to Auckland upzoning.
studies.limitation: Permits, not completions; international, broad reform.
studies.relevance: Quasi-experimental density evidence and candidate validation target; don't add to the 2025 synthetic-control estimate.

studies.title: Land-use reforms and housing costs: Does allowing for increased density lead to greater affordability?
studies.authors: Christina Plerhoples Stacy; Christopher Davis; Yonah Freemark; Lydia Lo; Graham MacDonald; Vivian Zheng; Rolf Pendall
studies.finding: Loosening reforms are associated with 0.8% higher housing supply after three to nine years, mostly at the higher end of the rent distribution (180 reforms, 1,136 cities).
studies.limitation: Fixed-effects association; not an isolated missing-middle effect; reform coding is ML/news-based and contested.
studies.relevance: Broad U.S. bracket for supply responses; do not assign the same 0.8% to every scenario.

studies.title: How Big Upzonings Affect Housing Supply: New York City and Philadelphia
studies.authors: Yipeng Su; Will Curran-Groome; Yonah Freemark
studies.finding: Over 4,000 additional NYC units within four years; Philadelphia effects are on permits and vary by time and neighborhood.
studies.limitation: NYC stock and Philadelphia permits are different outcomes; no significant response in some neighborhoods.
studies.relevance: Priority U.S. benchmark for substantial upzoning and heterogeneity.

studies.title: Upzoning Chicago: Impacts of a Zoning Reform on Property Values and Housing Construction
studies.finding: No detectable relative increase in new-unit permitting over five years on upzoned transit-area parcels.
studies.limitation: Context-specific null; density and parking changes bundled; author summary read.
studies.relevance: Important null result: test whether allowed density binds and pencils; legal capacity alone may not produce units in five years.

studies.title: Effects of Transit-Oriented Incentive Programs: Evidence from Los Angeles
studies.finding: LA's TOC program increased proposed units but had no observable effect on permitted units; an approval-risk model explains changes in project composition.
studies.limitation: Working paper; proposed units, permits and stock are distinct outcomes.
studies.relevance: Priority evidence for proposal-to-permit attrition near transit; follow the project pipeline.

studies.title: Los Angeles' Housing Crisis and Local Planning Responses: Inclusionary Zoning and the Transit-Oriented Communities Plan
studies.authors: Linna Zhu; Evgeny Burinskiy; Jorge De la Roca; Richard K. Green; Marlon G. Boarnet
studies.finding: TOC density/affordability packages can outperform market-rate-only development in some neighborhoods; take-up was substantial.
studies.limitation: Program take-up isn't net citywide supply.
studies.relevance: Template for transit density, affordability and feasibility interactions; pair with an uptake model.

studies.title: Minus Minimums
studies.finding: After Buffalo's 2017 citywide repeal, developers of 36 major projects made voluntary parking choices, often below the old minimums.
studies.limitation: Not a causal housing-unit estimate; journal full text access-blocked.
studies.relevance: Supports testing developer-provided parking assumptions.

studies.title: Parking policy: The effects of residential minimum parking requirements in Seattle
studies.authors: C.J. Gabbe; Gregory Pierce; Gordon Clowers
studies.finding: Across 868 developments (60,361 units), 40% less parking than earlier standards would have required; about 70% of projects without a minimum still supplied some parking.
studies.limitation: Parking outcome, not housing units.
studies.relevance: Endogenize voluntary parking; use parking choices and costs to change feasibility.

studies.title: The Housing Supply and Price Effects of Reducing Parking Requirements in U.S. Cities
studies.finding: City event study reports increased supply after parking reforms; no coefficient transcribed.
studies.limitation: Preliminary poster.
studies.relevance: High-priority full-paper request: directly addresses U.S. housing-unit outcomes.

studies.title: Impact fees and single-family home construction
studies.finding: Non-water/sewer impact fees increased construction for some size/location groups, consistent with infrastructure and approval mechanisms.
studies.limitation: Years and variable definitions not certified from the abstract.
studies.relevance: Counterweight to a cost-only fee effect; no universal inverse elasticity follows.

studies.title: The Effects of Impact Fees on Multifamily Housing Construction
studies.finding: Positive non-water/sewer associations in inner suburbs, negative water/sewer effects (Florida county panel).
studies.limitation: Draft not assumed identical to publication.
studies.relevance: Fee categories and mechanisms matter; not direct evidence for $50k to $25k.

studies.title: Do Development Impact Fees Reduce the Rate of Residential Development?
studies.finding: Impact fees reduced residential development rates by more than 25% (DuPage County, IL, 1977-1992).
studies.limitation: Old, local; a fee introduction isn't the inverse of halving current fees.
studies.relevance: Potential fee-sensitivity benchmark with limited transferability.

studies.title: Assessing the Cost of Impact Fees on Affordable Housing: LIHTC Projects in California
studies.authors: Carolina Reid; Leslye Corsiglia; Ben Metcalf
studies.finding: Average impact fees approached $20,000 per unit across 691 new-construction LIHTC projects (2020-2023).
studies.limitation: Funding-equivalence arithmetic, not a market-wide causal estimate.
studies.relevance: Observed per-unit fees; update the $50,000 assumption with local evidence.

studies.title: The Effects of Rent Control Expansion on Tenants, Landlords, and Inequality: Evidence from San Francisco
studies.authors: Rebecca Diamond; Tim McQuade; Franklin Qian
studies.finding: Affected landlords reduced rental supply by 15% through sales to owner-occupants and redevelopment.
studies.limitation: Rental tenure supply, not physical stock.
studies.relevance: Outside the five reforms; shows why tenure and physical stock are different outcomes.

studies.title: Do land use regulations stifle residential development? Evidence from California cities
studies.finding: Citation verified; findings not extracted.
studies.limitation: No numeric claims until primary text is reviewed.
studies.relevance: U.S. regulation-and-construction evidence to retrieve.

studies.title: Making housing affordable? The local effects of relaxing land-use regulation
studies.finding: Citation verified; findings not extracted.
studies.limitation: No estimates certified.
studies.relevance: International upzoning comparison to retrieve.

studies.title: The Effect of Rezoning on Local Housing Supply and Demand: Evidence from New York City
studies.finding: Increased housing supply in upzoned neighborhoods relative to adjacent areas, alongside mobility changes (2004-2013 rezonings).
studies.limitation: Findings attributed to the 2023 draft; no coefficient extracted.
studies.relevance: Spatial comparison design; reconcile with the published version.

studies.title: Crowd out effects of place-based subsidized rental housing: New evidence from the LIHTC program
studies.authors: Michael D. Eriksen; Stuart S. Rosenthal
studies.finding: Citation verified; findings not extracted.
studies.limitation: No crowd-out estimate extracted.
studies.relevance: Subsidized units are not automatically net additional homes.

studies.title: The effects of low income housing tax credit developments on neighborhoods
studies.finding: Citation verified; findings not extracted.
studies.limitation: Full text needed.
studies.relevance: Background on subsidy spillovers.

studies.title: The Integrated Housing Model Dashboard
studies.finding: Compares business-as-usual housing scenarios with supply and construction-productivity scenarios.
studies.limitation: Equations and data not extracted; Canadian assumptions.
studies.relevance: Example of a baseline vs. intervention scenario dashboard.

studies.title: Zoning in American Cities: Are Reforms Making a Difference? An AI-based Analysis
studies.finding: NLP on zoning documents from over 2,000 U.S. places; form-based code language is associated with denser form, more multifamily housing and walkability.
studies.limitation: Association, not a causal unit estimate.
studies.relevance: Extract baseline zoning rules at scale; validate against actual codes.

studies.title: Regulation and Frontier Housing Supply
studies.finding: Israel multifamily: mean regulatory tax 47% of price; minimum efficient scale about five floors.
studies.limitation: Strong identification assumptions; no per-policy effects.
studies.relevance: Structural approach to cost, height and regulatory constraints.

studies.title: Estimating the housing production function with unobserved land heterogeneity
studies.finding: Estimator for capital-land substitution with latent local conditions; Tokyo application.
studies.limitation: Methodological; calibrate U.S. parameters before use.
studies.relevance: Lets developers substitute capital for land when height/FAR rises.

studies.title: Housing Potential Common Data Model and City Digital Twin
studies.authors: Megan Katsumi; Mark Fox; Anderson Wong; Divnoor Chatha
studies.finding: Interoperable data model connecting zoning, land use, demographics and services.
studies.limitation: No causal construction effect.
studies.relevance: Schema for joining eligibility, parcel, market and transit inputs.

studies.title: Freeing the Law with LOCUS: A Local Ordinance Corpus for the United States
studies.authors: Denis Peskoff; Joe Barrow; Christopher Vu; Diag Davenport
studies.finding: Ordinance codes from 9,239 cities and counties with a county-harmonized layer for 2,309 counties.
studies.limitation: Corpus reuse terms unverified; validate extracted provisions and effective dates.
studies.relevance: Potential source for ADU, density, parking and fee rules.

studies.title: PolicySpace2: modeling markets and endogenous public policies
studies.finding: Open-source spatial ABM comparing housing acquisition, rental vouchers and cash aid.
studies.limitation: Model-dependent ranking; not a measured effect of the challenge reforms.
studies.relevance: Optional architecture for broader policy interactions.

studies.title: A Mediation Analysis of the Relationship Between Land Use Regulation Stringency and Employment Dynamics
studies.finding: WRLURI stringency and 2010-2020 sector employment across 878 jurisdictions.
studies.limitation: Employment, not housing units.
studies.relevance: Background only; do not use to predict production.

studies.title: Effectiveness of Rent Controls: Evidence from Spain
studies.finding: Catalonia's 2024 rent control: fewer tenancy agreements and less robust rent-growth reductions.
studies.limitation: Short follow-up; outside the five reforms.
studies.relevance: Methods template for a staggered state policy rollout.

studies.title: Can zoning reform increase housing construction? Evidence from Auckland
studies.finding: Synthetic control: Auckland's 2016 upzoning roughly doubled dwelling permits per capita within five years; about 52,200 additional permits over seven years (46% of 112,300).
studies.limitation: Permit/consent outcome despite 'starts' wording; overlaps the 2023 JUE paper.
studies.relevance: Upper-bound comparator for broad by-right upzoning; compare, don't add, with the 2023 estimate.

studies.title: Going it Alone: The Impact of Upzoning on Housing Construction in Lower Hutt
studies.finding: Three-to-fourfold per-capita consents after density and parking reforms; net regional starts up 12-17% after displacement.
studies.limitation: Consents proxy starts; bundled reforms.
studies.relevance: Priority evidence for regional displacement; not a parking-only effect.

studies.title: Dispelling myths: Reviewing the evidence on zoning reforms in Auckland
studies.finding: Reviews critiques of three Auckland studies and finds the supply and rent evidence robust.
studies.limitation: Review, not an independent estimate.
studies.relevance: Check control groups and objections; don't count as extra evidence.

studies.title: The Local Residential Land Use Regulatory Environment Across U.S. Housing Markets: Evidence from a New Wharton Index
studies.authors: Joseph Gyourko; Jonathan Hartley; Jacob Krimmel
studies.finding: Survey-based regulatory index for about 2,450 communities; the coasts are most regulated; impact-fee use fell from about 75% to 50% of places between 2006 and 2018.
studies.limitation: Index data terms unclear; cite published findings only.
studies.relevance: Context on which states are most constrained.

studies.title: Reply to 'A Critique of an Urban Studies Article on the Housing Supply Impact of Land Use Reforms'
studies.authors: Christina Plerhoples Stacy; Yonah Freemark; Lydia Lo
studies.finding: Explains the scope and ML/news-based coding of the 2023 study and concedes classification limits.
studies.limitation: A reply; keep linked to the 2023 study.
studies.relevance: Interpretation limits of the 0.8% estimate.

studies.title: The Missing Middle: A Comparative Analysis of ADU and SB 9 Development in Ontario and Other Southern California Cities
studies.authors: Rose Institute of State and Local Government (Claremont McKenna)
studies.venue: Report commissioned by the City of Ontario
studies.finding: 'SB 9 resulted in the construction of few new units, while ADU reforms led to a significant increase in construction.'
studies.limitation: Descriptive comparison of a few cities; commissioned.
studies.relevance: Supports a lower take-up rate for lot splits/duplexes than for ADUs.

studies.title: Minneapolis Land Use Reforms Offer a Blueprint for Housing Affordability
studies.venue: Pew article archived by the Minnesota Legislature
studies.finding: Minneapolis stock rose 12% (2017-2022) while rents rose 1%, against 4% and 14% elsewhere in Minnesota.
studies.limitation: Descriptive; doesn't isolate triplex legalization or parking repeal.
studies.relevance: Read alongside the Minneapolis Fed analysis; use a demand-adjusted counterfactual.

studies.title: We Zoned for Density and Got Higher House Prices: Supply and Price Effects of Upzoning over 20 Years
studies.finding: Tracks 25,775 sites in 19 Brisbane activity centres; extensive unused capacity despite repeated upzonings.
studies.limitation: Observational.
studies.relevance: Legal capacity need not become construction promptly; test demand and redevelopment thresholds.

studies.title: Unpacking supply and demand in rent trends since the Minneapolis 2040 Plan
studies.finding: Rent trends are consistent with a local 2020 demand shock; simultaneous changes complicate attribution to the plan.
studies.limitation: Rents, not units.
studies.relevance: Balances the Pew Minneapolis narrative; include demand and financing in validation.

studies.title: Impact Fees and Housing Affordability
studies.finding: Reviews fee incidence, prices and supply mechanisms.
studies.limitation: No new estimate used.
studies.relevance: Locate fee studies; separate infrastructure funding from direct cost effects.

studies.title: Parking the Minimum Parking Requirement: Evidence from Nine U.S. Cities
studies.finding: Responses depend on market demand and prior policy; low-parking-demand districts show larger reductions, some low-density cities little change.
studies.limitation: Parking outcome; full text not reviewed.
studies.relevance: Strong evidence for voluntary parking assumptions; not a unit coefficient.

studies.title: After the Minimum Parking Requirement: Parking Reform in a Small University City
studies.finding: 84% of 43 major developments provided less parking than the earlier requirements.
studies.limitation: Bundled with other policies.
studies.relevance: Mechanism evidence; not an isolated parking-only unit effect.

studies.title: Do Parking Standards Matter? Evaluating the London Parking Reform with a Matched Pair Approach
studies.finding: About 0.76 fewer parking spaces per dwelling in applications, about 49% of the earlier level.
studies.limitation: London also imposed maximums.
studies.relevance: How binding standards affect parking; don't convert to housing units.

studies.title: Do Parking Maximums Deter Housing Development?
studies.finding: Fewer developments with maximums in outer London, more (often car-free) in inner London.
studies.limitation: Parking caps, not minimum repeal.
studies.relevance: Contextual evidence until methods are reviewed.

studies.title: Parking Requirements and Housing Development
studies.finding: LA adaptive-reuse conversions under flexible/offsite parking; no isolated unit estimate extracted.
studies.limitation: Primary text blocked.
studies.relevance: Adaptive reuse and parking location rules matter.

studies.title: The effect of minimum parking requirements on the housing stock
studies.finding: Simulation for a Stockholm suburb: parking norms reduce housing stock by 1.2% and raise rents.
studies.limitation: Model result, local calibration, long-run horizon.
studies.relevance: Architecture linking parking costs to supply; recalibrate locally.

studies.title: No Such Thing as Free Parking: Construction Costs in 17 U.S. Cities
studies.finding: Parking construction-cost compilation across 17 cities; no number certified yet.
studies.limitation: Full report not reviewed.
studies.relevance: Priority input for the pro forma parking-cost module.

studies.title: The Impacts of Minimum Parking Requirements: A Research Synthesis
studies.finding: Emphasizes continued voluntary parking and context-dependent responses.
studies.limitation: Some conclusions rest on case evidence.
studies.relevance: Citation-chaining resource; don't double-count with underlying studies.

studies.title: Can Development Impact Fees Help Mitigate Urban Sprawl?
studies.finding: Albuquerque permit analysis over 21 years of geographically differentiated fees; no net-supply number certified.
studies.limitation: Results not fully extracted.
studies.relevance: Redistribution of permits is not increased regional production.

studies.title: An Empirical Investigation of the Effects of Impact Fees on Housing and Land Markets
studies.finding: Fees capitalize into housing and land values (Dade County, FL).
studies.limitation: Price incidence, not starts.
studies.relevance: Who absorbs fee relief; not a production elasticity.

studies.title: It All Adds Up: The Cost of Housing Development Fees in Seven California Cities
studies.finding: Documents fee-system variation and distortions from fee design.
studies.limitation: No causal coefficient; 2018 amounts.
studies.relevance: Template for collecting actual baseline fees; per-unit vs. per-area charging.

studies.title: Ask an expert: Why development charges make new homes more expensive in Canada
studies.finding: Halving development charges made about 5% more projects financially viable (modeled).
studies.limitation: Denominator is projects; modeled viability, not observed starts.
studies.relevance: Closest scenario analogue to the 50% fee cut; obtain the technical documentation.

studies.title: Yes, Literally In My Backyard: The Effect of Gently Upzoning Single-Family Neighborhoods
studies.finding: Positive differential response in ADU permitting in single-family vs. two/three-family zones after California reforms (LA, San Diego, SF, 2010-2022).
studies.limitation: Not peer reviewed; don't translate the zone-level coefficient into a parcel uptake rate.
studies.relevance: Most direct ADU policy-effect design; review parallel trends and permit classification first.

studies.title: Accessory Dwelling Units and the Preemption of Land Use Regulation
studies.finding: State ADU preemption varies across parking, review process, occupancy and other provisions.
studies.limitation: Statutory vintage; refresh before treating as current law.
studies.relevance: Specification for the policy-baseline database.

studies.title: Local Government Accessory Dwelling Unit Policies After State Preemption in California
studies.finding: No finding certified.
studies.limitation: Full text not retrieved.
studies.relevance: Implementation gap; not causal supply evidence.

studies.title: Financial Constraints and Housing Supply: Evidence from Seattle ADU Policy Reform
studies.finding: Abstract links ADU production after Seattle's 2019 reform to financing capacity.
studies.limitation: Seminar abstract; preliminary numbers not verified.
studies.relevance: High-priority paper request for uptake and financing.

studies.title: Under the (Neighbor)Hood: Understanding Interactions Among Zoning Regulations
studies.venue: Review of Economics and Statistics (accepted; DOI 10.1162/REST.a.1736)
studies.finding: Looser density restrictions, alone or with other relaxations, are most effective for supply and per-unit prices/rents (Greater Boston boundary design).
studies.limitation: Long-run boundary differences; TOD counterfactuals are modeled.
studies.relevance: Highest-priority interaction study: model the binding constraint, don't multiply independent effects.

studies.title: State Preemption in Theory and Practice: The Case of Parking Requirements
studies.finding: Heterogeneous local responses to California's 2022 parking preemption: supportive, strategically supportive, resistant.
studies.limitation: No unit coefficient.
studies.relevance: State adoption doesn't imply uniform local treatment; model compliance scenarios.

studies.title: Streamlining Multifamily Housing Production in California: Progress Implementing SB 35
studies.finding: 156 approved or pending projects comprising over 18,000 proposed units (2018-2021), mostly affordable.
studies.limitation: Pipeline counts, not net additional completions.
studies.relevance: Approval speed and funding interactions.

studies.title: San Diego's Success in Spurring Missing Middle Housing: The ADU Bonus Program
studies.finding: Local incentives and implementation interact with statewide ADU permission.
studies.limitation: No causal net-supply effect; 2023 rules.
studies.relevance: ADU/density interaction case and project-option design.

studies.title: The effects of government interventions on housing markets: A meta study of empirical literature
studies.finding: Synthesis of 1,077 studies; direct interaction research is sparse.
studies.limitation: Cross-study correlations are not causal interaction coefficients.
studies.relevance: Citation chaining; don't pool unlike outcomes.

studies.title: From Parking to Housing (Syracuse parking reform thesis)
studies.finding: Describes a matched difference-in-differences around a 2011 parking reform; nothing verified.
studies.limitation: Retrieval returned 403; no estimate asserted.
studies.relevance: Acquire and inspect before any use.

pilot_states.rationale: HCD Annual Progress Reports link policy changes to applications, permits and completions; most ADU and missing-middle evidence is Californian.
Greater Boston replication materials (Kulka, Sood, Chiumenti) and MassGIS.
Documented, freely downloadable statewide parcel dataset for building the eligibility component.
Team home state (memo); NYC PLUTO and Housing Database.
